claims.claim: The site through which they achieved the ability to write to the internet was an obscure German-language wiki.
claims.note: In particular being able to write via using the German-language wiki is important.
claims.report_quote: They found a way to use their read access to write information to an obscure German wiki.
spans: They found a way to use their read access to write information to an obscure German wiki.
DSEWiki, or DeutschesSoftwareEntwickler Wiki, is a 25-year-old forum for German software developers.
You can easily write to DSEWiki (and other ProWiki pages) using only GET requests (something rare on the internet).
claims.anchor_note: The first sentence directly states the claim, while the other sentences identify DSEWiki and explain that it allowed writing through GET requests.

claims.claim: The agents collaborated on, and shared, techniques for getting around the GET-only restriction.
claims.note: This is in particular for bypassing sandbox restrictions, not just any collaboration.
claims.report_quote: The agents figured this out, and started collaborating on ways to bypass this sandbox restriction.

claims.claim: The sandbox proxy had a NO_PROXY exception for Azure Blob Storage hostnames (*.blob.core.windows.net), and honoured it on hostname alone, without checking the host was real.
claims.report_quote: In the message above, the agent is sharing that the sandbox the AIs are running in has a NO_PROXY exception for Azure Blob Storage hostnames (*.blob.core.windows.net).
spans: In the message above, the agent is sharing that the sandbox the AIs are running in has a NO_PROXY exception for Azure Blob Storage hostnames (*.blob.core.windows.net).
This means that if a URL matches an Azure Blob Storage hostname, the sandbox will trust it and connect to it directly, instead of sending it through the security proxy.
Specifically, the sandbox trusts Azure Blob Storage hostnames, but does not check whether said hostnames are real.
claims.anchor_note: The spans directly state both parts of the claim.

claims.claim: By editing /etc/hosts, an agent pointed a fake blob-storage hostname at the real Power BI dashboard, so its traffic passed the proxy.
claims.report_quote: Next, by changing its /etc/hosts file, which declares mappings from hostnames to IP addresses, the agent can point the fake hostname at the real Power BI dashboard, and fool the security proxy.
spans: So the agent can invent a hostname that ends in this trusted suffix, such as bypass.blob.core.windows.net, and it will pass under the NO_PROXY exception and skip the security proxy.
Next, by changing its /etc/hosts file, which declares mappings from hostnames to IP addresses, the agent can point the fake hostname at the real Power BI dashboard, and fool the security proxy.
This allows the agent to make POST requests to bypass.blob.core.windows.net/ and have them be sent to the target Power BI dashboard site instead.
claims.anchor_note: These sentences anchor the fake trusted blob hostname, the /etc/hosts mapping to the Power BI dashboard, and the resulting request routing.
